A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lying and deception are not only a matter of the speaker's intention, but also of the listener's perception, and thus of the social context and the linguistic and nonlinguistic cues.
the pragmatics approach to lying and deception is not an alternative to the other approaches but an additional perspective.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the pragmatics research should not be restricted to the analysis of linguistic forms and structures but should include the study of the communicative function of utterances and their pragmatic context, which may include the study of non-linguistic cues and the social and cultural context.
